title: C1691 — Fuel pressure sensor connector reference
introduction:
This sheet is titled as a fuel pressure sensor reference, but a circuit-function entry identifies an engine-oil-level sensor. I keep that disagreement front and center: a neat connector drawing cannot settle a disputed name tag. The component identity needs review before treating these assignments as a confirmed fuel-pressure-sensor map.

You can still learn how the reference is organized. Compare the connector metadata with the housing illustration, match a printed cavity label to its table row, and read the circuit fields together. The pigtail table separately associates a kit with its service part and engineering shell.

This is a reference-reading guide. It supplies no physical access, release, probing, pressure measurement or replacement procedure. Physical viewing direction, gauge conventions and the Size and Used codes are unspecified.

edits.why: The drawing has vertically arranged cavity labels, a broad housing projection on the left and a smaller projection on the right. I use those visible features to navigate the printed view. They establish neither release movements nor which physical side of the connector the reader would face.

Read across each cavity’s row to keep circuit identity, color, gauge and function associated. The function wording distinguishes a sensor connection, a powertrain signal return and a voltage reference, but the sensor description conflicts with the page title. Preserve the engine-reference qualifiers exactly as printed; they do not establish engine applicability or a voltage test value.

Keep the kit’s service-part and engineering-shell fields together when reading its catalog entry. The pigtail gauge and circuit-row gauges describe their respective entries; their difference alone supplies no wire-selection or splicing rule. The image filename refers to a separate image. Catalog agreement cannot resolve the disputed sensor identity.

originalAuthorHold: The title and metadata identify a FUEL PRESSURE SENSOR, while a pin-function entry identifies SENSOR - LOW LEVEL ENGINE OIL. Review is required to establish which component description and circuit assignments belong together.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all31 primary units, both complete source pages and sole figure, and3 edits. Fuel-pressure title versus literal low-engine-oil-level function identity ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
